about: The component manifest: one entry per part of the model and per tool, shared by the Architecture page and the test registry (the operator's recovery directive of Oct 5, 2026, sections 7C and 9). The fields and the check are described in Source/Python/mimo_bridge/tools/component_manifest.py. id, name, does, paths, blocks, flags and aliases are typed; last code change, last independent QA, QA STALE, switch state, open defects and linked tests are computed and are not in this file.

scope.about: Model code is every .py file under Source/Python/lem and Source/Python/mimo_bridge that the trainer imports, directly or through other imports, plus the files under 'also' (the tools' own files). The check fails when one of them is mapped to no component.

components.name: simulated world
components.does: MuJoCo advances the crib scene (the infant body, the toys, the mobile, the walls) by 5 physics steps of 10 ms per model step from the joint torques it is given, and returns the body's joint, contact, camera and head-sensor readings.

confirmed.basis: Release-only edit checked (Oct 24, 2026): mimo_bridge/env.py BridgeEnv.__init__ re-roots its run_dir with repo_paths.localize before writing the scene files (a saved world names D:/UEMA_scratch/...; MuJoCo's C code opens those files). A run_dir that is not a recorded folder is unchanged. The rest of the mapped code is the development repository's at 9916126d1 with a copyright line added; the entry's description stands.

components.name: caregiver (the world's adult)
components.does: A scripted program of the world that reads the infant's gaze direction and contacts and, from its saved random state, moves the adult figure, brings and removes toys and plays recorded speech into the audio input.

confirmed.basis: carried over from the explainer's text, not checked against the code

components.name: sensory frame packing
components.does: Packs each body's sense readings into one 31,040-byte frame per model step in the byte layout of the model's tokenizer, and builds from the frames of all bodies the per-sense input tensors the encoders receive.

confirmed.basis: checked against the code change only: ca77bb8d0 (the only commit since 22c27490c that changed the mapped code) added training_source_masks to lem/source_mask.py, which reduces the per-sample source labels to one label per sense for the current batch and one for the target batch; its only caller is lem/training_step.py, outside this trainer's import closure; frame_encoder.py, datasource.py and LemLite._batch_frames are unchanged; the entry's text still holds (the sentence itself was carried over from the explainer's text and was not re-read against frame_encoder.py or datasource.py).

components.name: vision input
components.does: Cuts each eye's two camera pictures (a wide view and a narrow centre view) into patches of 16 x 16 pixels and outputs them as the rows the vision encoder receives.

confirmed.basis: carried over from the explainer's text, not checked against the code

components.name: tactile input
components.does: Turns MuJoCo's contacts and the body's skin points into up to 32 rows per body (pressure, area, place and the touching part) that the tactile encoder receives.

confirmed.basis: carried over from the explainer's text, not checked against the code

components.name: audio input
components.does: Builds each ear's spectrum (256 frequency bands from 40 Hz to 8 kHz, as a log level) from the world's events and the caregiver's speech, and outputs the two spectra and the ear-difference numbers the audio encoder receives.

confirmed.basis: carried over from the explainer's text, not checked against the code

components.name: proprioception input
components.does: Reads each tracked body part's position, orientation and velocities from MuJoCo and outputs one row per body handle that the proprioception encoder receives.

confirmed.basis: carried over from the explainer's text, not checked against the code

components.name: motor input (the executed command fed back)
components.does: Takes the command the body executed in the last model step (26 body handles x 9 numbers, positions divided by 200 cm) with the achieved pose and outputs the rows the motor encoder receives.

confirmed.basis: carried over from the explainer's text, not checked against the code

components.name: vestibular input
components.does: Builds a vector of 29 numbers per body from the head's accelerometer and gyro, the neck, the support contacts and the joints' efforts and limits, which the vestibular encoder receives.

components.name: motor encoder
components.does: A per-row MLP, attention between the 26 body-handle rows of the executed command and one learned pooling query, which together output one motor token per body per model step; under --attention-cap on (ATTENTION_CAP) its 2 attention layers and its pool score each handle as a bound times the cosine of query and key.

components.name: encoder registry and shared output normalization
components.does: Builds the active senses' encoders from the resolved configuration, runs each on its input, and passes every token through one shared normalization layer (subtract the token's own mean, divide by its own spread).

components.name: top-down gate
components.does: Per sense, mixes a learned share g (0 to 50 parts in 100) of the model's own prediction of this model step into the encoder's token, g x prediction + (1 - g) x token, and outputs the mixed tokens that acting, planning and the goal ring read; every lesson grades the raw encoder tokens.

components.name: transformer (the core)
components.does: Lines up the senses' tokens of the newest and the remembered model steps with learned sense and time embeddings, passes them through the core's blocks (three attention stages and a feed-forward network each) and a final normalization, and outputs one state vector per token for the heads, the motor controller and the planner; under --attention-cap on (ATTENTION_CAP) the cross-modal attention of every block scores each key as a bound times the cosine of its query and key.

components.name: prediction heads
components.does: One head per sense except motor (a learned query, attention over the transformer's output and a 2-layer MLP) that outputs that sense's token for the next model step, 50 ms ahead.

components.name: training lessons and their weights
components.does: Weights each sense's lesson by whether its input is real, stale or synthetic, divides each sense's next-step error by its own no-change error when --next-frame-norm persistence is set, sums the lessons into the loss and clips the gradient before the optimizer's update.

components.name: imagination chain
components.does: Starting from the oldest model step the chain keeps, predicts the next model step's tokens, feeds that prediction back in as input and predicts again, --imagination-steps times; each predicted step's error against the raw tokens that arrived is added to the loss, and nothing is sent to the body.

components.name: replay memory
components.does: Stores each model step's tokens, executed command and achieved pose per body (--replay-size model steps) and, every --replay-every model steps, draws a batch of stored windows and runs the lessons on them as one more optimizer update.

components.name: motor controller
components.does: An MLP with a confidence head that takes the transformer's pooled output, the body handles' current state and the gradient of wellness with respect to that state, and outputs the command: 26 body handles x 9 numbers (target position, orientation as 4 numbers, radius, strength 0 to 1).

components.name: command execution path
components.does: Takes a proposed command and outputs what the body receives: the phase's limits on strength and on the position step from the present pose, the eyes' row as sent, a blend of --smooth-actions of the new command with the rest of the previous one, then the action decoder's conversion of the 26 handle targets into joint torques; with --finger-joint-servo on (FINGER_JOINT_SERVO) each finger hinge is stepped toward its own latched goal angle instead of toward the fingertip's pose.

components.name: gaze command

components.name: planner goal distance
components.does: Per body: for each real sense except motor, the mean squared difference between the predicted next token and the goal's token, summed over those senses with equal weights, plus the effort term (the strength regulariser x the sum of the squared strengths); it is the quantity the search lowers.

components.name: head-tilt repair (the vestibular input path)
components.does: With --vestibular-input-path on or on_delayed_encoder_only, per body and model step the vestibular encoder's 28 input numbers (each minus its running mean, divided by its running spread, clipped to -4 to +4) pass through one Linear(28 -> 192) without bias, times 1/sqrt(28); the result u is added to the encoder's last-layer output v as v + s x u, s being the standard deviation of v over its 192 numbers, before the shared normalization (one forward hook on the encoder). The weight is zero at the switch, so the first tokens equal those without the path. On a training model step's live call, when the largest row's u has a root mean square above three tenths, the whole weight is multiplied by three tenths over that size; on every call a row whose u is above three tenths is scaled back to three tenths. Under on the delayed next-model-step lesson trains neither the encoder's own layers nor the path (the previous row's vestibular token enters it without gradient); under on_delayed_encoder_only it trains the encoder's layers and not the path. Its purpose: a token that carries head tilt, which the trained encoder's last layer does not pass on.

components.does: With --finger-joint-servo on (it needs --hand-target-mode wrist_relative_v1), the action decoder steps each finger hinge toward its own latched goal angle, dq = goal - angle read from the physics state (the 44 hinge goals per body the planner search and the hand stage chose, HandTargetControl.goals_by_joint), in place of the damped least squares toward the fingertip's pose; the hinge range clip, u = strength x (6 x dq - 0.3 x hinge speed), one shared factor per finger chain so no command passes its limit, the final clip and the coupling tendons stay as they are. The world then reports the motor contract with finger_joint_servo_v1, replay stores and samples those model steps under contract bit 32 apart from the others, the transition's action contract gains that part, and the trainer refuses worlds whose rule differs from the launch's. With --hand-goals memory the hand stage's fixed response must declare the rule it was fit under, in both directions (the admitted fit is the pose servo's), and the probe harness refuses a world running another rule than its learner. Its purpose: the finger command means each hinge's goal in the planner search, the hand stage, the decoder and the stored rows alike. Off (the default) every changed line computes production's numbers.

confirmed.basis: checked against the code change only: ca77bb8d0 (the only commit since 76336d264 that changed its wiring) changed the wiring part LemLite.replay_update only by marking the forward model's embedding cache stale after optimizer.step(); the replay contract's finger servo bit (replay_contract with finger_joint_servo) is unchanged; the entry's text still holds.
